success.description: The full author version explicitly states whole secret-key recovery success1 for full 14-round AES256 independent-biclique search, using complete key-space group coverage. Section8.4/PDF20 binds this rate to the corresponding construction and source D/T/M row. The proceedings explicitly delegates this exact Table1 row to the full version, whose Table1 matches its rounds, construction, D/T-normalized/M and biclique length. The stored time is computations/success-rate; at claimed success1 the normalization does not change its value. The full source has unresolved internal cost formulas, attached as a time-field conflict; the claimed success1 does not establish that the headline budget is achievable. This event is not merely conditional biclique closure and is not compression-preimage success. The acquired mirror is separately hashed; exact official-byte identity and historical availability remain unauthenticated, so no frontier or full-audit certification follows.

review.scope: Source extraction, direct proceedings-to-full-version endpoint bridge and success/cost normalization independently checked. Verified denotes extraction applicability, not attack execution, mathematical certification of an author model, resolution of cost conflicts or a completed full-paper/forward audit.

field_conflicts.label: Full-version AES-256 headline versus detailed cost formulas
field_conflicts.description: The proceedings Table1 endpoint explicitly refers to the full version. That full edition states whole-key success1, but Table5 prints total2^254.64 and recomputation2^14.64 while Table1 and Section8.4 print2^254.42 and2^14.383. Section8.4 says5.4375 SubBytes but substitutes5.625/17.25. Preserve the proceedings2^254.42 and the author success claim; no exact achievable cost is certified or repaired.
